question: What approximate percentage of total waste generated by health care facilities is classified as hazardous?
explanation: While the vast majority of hospital waste is general refuse, roughly fifteen percent requires specialized hazardous handling due to infectious or toxic properties. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: Why is the proper management of health care waste considered an urgent public health priority in many developing regions?

options.A: General waste constantly transforms into radioactive material
options.B: Hospitals generate more hazardous waste than urban households
options.C: International agencies mandate strict financial penalties for spills
options.D: Deficient infrastructure and budget limits threaten safe handling

explanation: Weak infrastructure and financial limitations in regions like Sub-Saharan Africa make standard waste processing exceptionally difficult, amplifying public health risks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: Which waste category includes discarded needles, scalpels, and broken ampoules?
explanation: Sharps refer specifically to items capable of puncturing or cutting the skin, requiring puncture-proof containers for immediate disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: What is the primary operational reason for classifying health care waste into specific categories?

options.A: Ensuring all discarded items can be safely recycled into household goods
options.B: Reducing the total volume of materials produced by surgical wards
options.C: Preventing hazardous materials from mixing with ordinary refuse
options.D: Complying with international trade tariffs on medical supplies

explanation: Segregation into clear categories keeps dangerous infectious or toxic elements separate from general household-type trash. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: What is a primary occupational risk associated with poorly managed sharp instruments in a hospital setting?

options.A: Allergic skin reactions to latex gloves
options.B: Severe radiation sickness from diagnostic equipment
options.D: Chronic respiratory failure from paper dust inhalation

explanation: Exposed needles and sharps present an immediate physical hazard that can transmit serious infections like HIV and hepatitis. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: A patient living near an open hospital dump develops chronic respiratory issues from toxic smoke. Which practice most likely caused this exposure?

options.A: Leaching of heavy metals into groundwater
options.C: Improper storage of liquid pharmaceutical waste
options.D: Accidental puncture from a contaminated scalpel

explanation: Open-air incineration of medical plastics releases hazardous air pollutants like dioxins and furans, harming nearby residents. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: Which international body publishes widely recognized guidance manuals on safe health care waste management practices?
explanation: The World Health Organization creates authoritative guidelines and technical handbooks used globally to improve medical waste protocols. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of the Basel Convention regarding global waste management?

options.A: Determining clinical diagnostic criteria for infectious diseases
options.B: Enforcing mandatory vaccination schedules for healthcare workers
options.C: Regulating the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
options.D: Setting financial budgets for hospital construction projects

explanation: The Basel Convention prevents industrialized nations from exporting their hazardous waste to countries with weaker regulatory infrastructures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: At what point in the workflow should health care waste segregation take place?
explanation: Sorting waste immediately where it is produced is vital to ensure correct classification and minimize handling risks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: When should a puncture-resistant sharps container be sealed and removed from a clinical ward?

options.A: At the end of every calendar month
options.B: Only when it is completely packed to the brim
options.D: Immediately after a single needle is dropped inside

explanation: Sealing containers at three-quarters capacity prevents accidental overfilling and reduces puncture injuries during handling. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which an autoclave neutralizes infectious waste?
explanation: Autoclaves use high-pressure steam to effectively kill microorganisms and pathogens present in medical waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: Which technology destroys pathogens and reduces waste volume through high-temperature burning, but requires strict air filtration?
explanation: Incineration uses high heat to destroy waste completely, but poor filtration can release toxic smoke and pollutants into the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: What is a key daily responsibility of nursing professionals regarding health care waste on a hospital ward?

options.A: Monitoring and modeling correct segregation practices
options.C: Transporting bulk incinerator ash to municipal sites

explanation: Nurses oversee ward operations and must demonstrate proper sorting techniques to protect themselves and their colleagues. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)

question: A ward nurse notices that sharps containers are consistently overflowing before collection. What is the most appropriate professional action to take?

options.A: Report the hazard to facility management and request prompt replacement
options.B: Wait until the end of the month for scheduled maintenance
options.C: Instruct patients to push the needles down manually to save space
options.D: Mix the overflow into standard black general waste bags

explanation: Reporting safety breaches to management ensures corrective administrative action is taken before injuries occur. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)

question: What is a common obstacle to effective medical waste management in resource-limited health care settings?

options.A: Excessive enforcement of international trade laws
options.B: Chronic shortages of financial budgets and supplies
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of high-tech incinerators
options.D: Mandatory compliance with nuclear safety boards

explanation: Financial constraints often result in a lack of basic operational supplies like proper bags, protective gear, and functioning equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h8)

question: Which strategy is most essential for improving waste handling practices among support staff in underfunded clinics?

options.A: Importing expensive automated sorting machinery from overseas
options.B: Implementing pragmatic, continuous staff education programs
options.C: Imposing heavy salary deductions for minor sorting mistakes
options.D: Eliminating the use of disposable medical equipment entirely

explanation: Regular, practical training helps staff understand biohazard risks and ensures proper adherence even when resources are scarce. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h8)
